Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
534 of 2023 at Police Station- Akbarpur, District- Kanpur Dehat under Sections 366, 376 IPC.

entities.text: Police Station- Akbarpur, District- Kanpur Dehat
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 27.12.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 14.03.2024.

The following arguments made by Sri Deepak Kumar Verma, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Chandan Agarwal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Arshad vs State Of U.P. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128667945/
1
1. The victim and the applicant were intimate who had eloped together.
2. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.
3. The applicant works for the victim's father as a truck driver.
4. The victim in her statement under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
She has also stated that she planned to get married to the applicant.
Lastly the victim has asserted that she had consensual physical relations with the applicant.

5. The victim has not made any allegation of commission of rape, abduction or forceful assault against the applicant in her statement under Sections 161 CrPC and 164 CrPC.
6.
The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.

7. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C.
and Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
8. Medical evidence to establish the commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
10. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Arshad be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
Arshad vs State Of U.P. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128667945/

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Order Date :- 15.5.2024
